round_interpretation: All 11 audited historical masks have complete three-seed evidence. The compact four-local plus four-credit/inflation/curve model has IC 0.263889, NLL -1.753270, and conventional Sharpe 1.435086; the two larger frontier points offer only small aggregate NLL improvements at much lower IC/Sharpe. Only one exact one-feature pair exists in the historical U.S. panel. Therefore the first round tests each of the compact parent's eight non-time inputs individually, then explores lag, task-specific volatility, oil return, and a transferable alternative local basis. Retain all Pareto tradeoffs rather than declaring the compact parent a universal winner or treating NLL as a veto.
default_expected_tradeoff: Evaluate IC, Gaussian NLL, conventional Sharpe, seed dispersion, and coverage. Input count is reported, not a fourth objective; narrower forecasts alone are not a benefit.
default_falsification: A dominated result with no competitive simplification does not support this hypothesis. A new nondominated tradeoff remains evidence even if it differs from the expected direction.

candidates.name: compact_without_mom6m
candidates.hypothesis: Skip-month annual momentum, rank and slope may preserve useful local trend information without six-month momentum; this is an untested exact removal from the new compact front.

candidates.name: compact_without_skip_month_momentum
candidates.hypothesis: Six-month momentum and the remaining local features may substitute for the reconstructed annual skip-month predictor in this macro context; do not assume its selected presence proves necessity.

candidates.name: compact_without_cross_sectional_rank
candidates.hypothesis: The fixed 15-task momentum rank may be redundant with local momentum and macro state for a four-task U.S. equity model; test rather than infer a universally needed rank input.

candidates.name: compact_without_trend_slope
candidates.hypothesis: Dimensionless momentum may suffice without the absolute-price slope, reducing representation complexity while retaining the credit/inflation state.

candidates.name: compact_without_cpi_year_change
candidates.hypothesis: Credit-spread state and the yield curve may make the annual CPI signal unnecessary for the compact parent's ranking advantage; this must be checked on repaired, nonzero inflation values.

candidates.name: compact_without_hy_change
candidates.hypothesis: The HY z-score may carry enough credit information without the one-month HY change; the new genuine historical observations make this a meaningful conditional credit test.

candidates.name: compact_without_hy_zscore
candidates.hypothesis: The HY change may substitute for the standardized spread state; comparing this with the reciprocal removal will identify whether the two credit representations are complementary.

candidates.name: compact_without_curve_spread
candidates.hypothesis: The CPI and credit signals may provide the relevant macro regime without the Treasury curve spread, or its removal may establish a broadly useful curve input.

candidates.name: compact_plus_recent_return_lag
candidates.hypothesis: Lagged realized excess return could have different value in the new compact credit model than in the weak local-only pair; test its conditional value without requiring its removal.

candidates.name: compact_plus_local_realized_volatility
candidates.hypothesis: A single task-level realized-volatility input may recover the larger volatility model's small density advantage without importing its entire extra feature block.

candidates.name: compact_plus_oil_return
candidates.hypothesis: Oil return might transfer useful commodity information from international equity contexts into the compact U.S. credit model without adding a gold/oil ratio or a broad commodity bundle.

candidates.name: compact_macro_with_transferable_local_basis
candidates.hypothesis: An alternative four-input local basis may preserve the compact macro model's advantage and offer a shared representation across equity and fixed-income tasks; this is not inferred from inclusion frequency.
